runs.text: Q1. How is the idea of an object in programming related to objects in a database?

Ans: In programming, anything in the world, such as a car, a bus or a human being, is considered an object, and an object has properties and behaviour. In a database, anything that lies inside the database is called a database object. The database itself i

s an object, and tables, views, stored procedures and functions are objects created inside it. In general terms, the elements within a table, such as its columns and rows, are also spoken of as objects. The idea of an object is similar, but database object
s are not the objects of a programming language.
Q2. Where does a database live?
Ans: A database lives on the database server. The server holds the DBMS, and the DBMS holds the databases. It can be a relational or a non-relational DBMS, and in both cases t
he databases are stored on the server. The server is the highest level in the hierarchy of everything that is created and stored.
Q3. What is a schema in MySQL?
Ans: In MySQL a schema and a database are the same thing, so the list that Workbench shows unde

r Schemas is the list of the databases of the server. Some other database systems treat a schema as a separate level that is used to group and categorise the databases or the objects. With MySQL, the words schema and database can be used for the same objec
t.
Q4. What is the hierarchy of database objects, from the server down to the data?
Ans: The server holds the databases, which are also called schemas. A database holds objects such as tables, views, stored procedures and functions. A table has columns and

rows. The data that is inserted is stored in the cells of the rows, under the columns. The hierarchy is therefore server, database (schema), table (or another object), columns and rows, and finally the data.
Q5. What does the database check when an INSERT
INTO statement is executed?

Ans: The statement is not executed directly on the data. The DBMS works down the hierarchy, and it checks in which database the object is, then which table, then which column is to receive the value, and then which row the valu
e belongs to. After all of this is resolved, the value is stored in that place. Many such steps happen internally for a single statement.
Q6. What is a view, and can data be stored in a view?
Ans: A view is a database object that sits at the same level of

the hierarchy as a table, and it also shows rows and columns. Data cannot be stored in a view. Only a table stores data, so a view is not used to store the data that is inserted. A view is created with the CREATE command, in the same way as a table is crea
ted, and the SELECT command is used to read from it. The exact difference between a table and a view is studied separately.
Q7. Which commands change a structure or data that has already been created?
Ans: ALTER changes a table that exists, and DROP remove

s a database or another object. These are DDL commands. UPDATE changes the values that are already stored in a table, and DELETE removes values. These are DML commands. The commands used so far are CREATE and INSERT, and SELECT for reading. In interviews,
the questions asked are the difference between DELETE and DROP and the difference between UPDATE and ALTER, and each of these commands is studied separately.
Q8. What are the three layers of a DBMS?
Ans: A DBMS is organised into three layers. The first is

the physical layer, where the data is actually stored and which is managed by the database administrator. The second is the logical layer, also called the conceptual layer, where tables, relationships, functions, views and procedures are created, and where
developers work. The third is the view layer, also called the external layer, which is used by the end users who only look at the data.
Q9. What is the physical layer of a DBMS, and who manages it?

Ans: The physical layer is the lowest layer, and it is where the data is stored in reality. It consists of the data files, the data blocks, the catalogues, the logs and the cache. It is created by the DBMS at the time a database is created and installed. I
t is managed completely by one person, the database administrator (DBA). A developer is a user of the DBMS and does not have to create files, catalogues or logs or to manage them.
Q10. What are the system databases of MySQL, and what do they contain?
Ans:

A MySQL server contains databases that were not created by the developer. They are created automatically when MySQL is installed, and the databases are information_schema, mysql, performance_schema and sys. They hold the information of the DBMS itself, suc

h as user accounts and their privileges, connections, status, performance reports and logs, and details of the databases, tables and columns. They belong to the physical layer, and they should not be changed. They can be queried with SELECT like any other
database.
Sample Input: No input
Sample Output:
0 row(s) affected
ENGINE | SUPPORT | COMMENT | TRANSACTIONS | XA | SAVEPOINTS
The result grid lists the storage engines that are available on the server. Its row
s depend on the installation, and nothing has been created by the developer in this database.
Q11. What is the logical layer of a DBMS, and who works in it?
Ans: The logical layer, also called the conceptual layer, is the layer above the physical layer. It

contains the tables, the relationships between the tables (primary keys and foreign keys), the functions, the views and the procedures. It is the layer in which a developer works: a web developer, an app developer, a data scientist or a data engineer. The

work done so far, such as creating databases and tables, applying constraints and inserting data, belongs to this layer. A developer works with the concepts of this layer and not with the files of the physical layer.
Q12. What is the view layer of a DBMS,
and who uses it?

Ans: The view layer is the top layer, also called the external layer. It is used by the end users of the data, such as a customer, a financial analyst, a business analyst or the head of a department. They only view the data and cannot cha

nge it. They do not need to know about tables, functions or relationships. A developer writes the query that fetches the data they ask for, for example all the employees of an organisation, and the result can be given to them as a report, such as a CSV fil
e. The person who receives it only views the report.
Q13. What is abstraction, and which layer of a DBMS has the highest abstraction?
Ans: Abstraction means hiding the implementation details and giving only what is needed to use something. A driver of a ca

r sits in the driver's seat, starts the engine and presses the pedals. The driver does not need to know how the engine, the gears or the fuel supply work, so for the driver the details are hidden. The engineers who build the car need to know every one of t

hese details. In a DBMS the physical layer has the lowest abstraction, as it deals with all the implementation details. The view layer has the highest abstraction, because the end users see only the data and nothing about how it is stored.
Q14. Compare the
physical layer, the logical layer and the view layer of a DBMS.
Ans: The physical layer holds the data files, blocks, catalogues, logs and cache, it is managed by the database administrator, and it has the lowest abstraction. The logical layer holds the t

ables, relationships, functions, views and procedures, it is used by developers such as web developers, app developers, data scientists and data engineers, and it is the concept level. The view layer is what the end users such as customers, financial analy
sts and business analysts see, it is only for viewing the data, and it has the highest abstraction.
Q15. What is a common table expression (CTE), and which types are there?
Ans: A CTE is a named result that is defined at the beginning of a query with the W

ITH keyword and is then used in the main query. It is used to reduce the redundancy and the complexity of a query, because the logic is written once and then reused. There are two types. A standalone CTE is independent and does not depend on another CTE. A
nested CTE is a CTE that is built on another CTE.
Q16. What is the difference between a subquery and a CTE?
Ans: Both are techniques for reducing the complexity of a query. A subquery is written inside the main query and cannot be reused, so the same logi
c has to be written again wherever it is needed. A CTE is defined once with WITH, and its name can be used many times in the main query.
Q17. Write a query that segments customers into High, Medium and Low using a CTE and a CASE WHEN statement based on their total sales.

Ans: The CTE calculates the total sales of every customer with SUM and GROUP BY. The main query reads the CTE and uses CASE WHEN to assign the segment. In this example, a total above 100 is High, a total from 50 to 100 is Medium and a total below 50 is Low

blocks.text:
WITH customer_sales AS (
SELECT customer_id, SUM(sales) AS total_sales
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT customer_id,
total_sales,
CASE
WHEN total_sales > 100 THEN 'High'
WHEN total_sales >= 50 THEN 'Medium'
ELSE 'Low'
END AS segment
FROM customer_sales;

runs.text: Sample Input: orders table with the columns order_id, customer_id and sales (other columns are not used)
order_id | customer_id | sales
Sample Output:
customer_id | total_sales | segment
1 | 130 | High
3 | 65 | Medium
